title: 2005 HMMT February Team Round 2 Problem 14
statement: Suppose that \(S\) tiles the set of all integer cubes. Prove that \(S\) has only one element.

solutions.text: Let the difference between the smallest and largest element of \(S\) be \(a\). Then the set equivalent to \(S\) that contains \(b^{3}\) can only contain integers between \(b^{3}-a\) and \(b^{3}+a\), inclusive. But for sufficiently large \(b, b^{3}\) is the only cube in this range, so \(S\) can only have one element.
